title: Conveyancing Paralegal
description:

title: Legal Administrator
description:
Legal Administrator - Property

Location: Marlborough, Wiltshire; office-based

Salary: £28-32 K plus excellent benefits package

About the Opportunity

Our client is a prestigious specialist law firm based in Marlborough, recognised for its high professional standards, client-focused approach and collaborative working environment.

An excellent opportunity has arisen for an experienced Legal Administrator to join its Property team, providing administrative and secretarial support across a varied portfolio of agricultural, commercial and residential property matters.

Key Requirements

You will be an organised, proactive and detail-oriented Legal Administrator with experience supporting legal professionals, ideally within a property or conveyancing environment.

You will bring:
- Previous experience in legal administration, legal secretarial support or property/conveyancing administration
- Experience supporting residential, commercial, agricultural or rural property transactions would be particularly advantageous
- Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise competing deadlines
- Excellent document production, proofreading and attention to detail
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, with the ability to learn legal practice and case management systems
- Confident, professional communication skills when dealing with clients, solicitors and external advisers
- A positive, flexible and collaborative approach to supporting fee earners within a small team
- High levels of discretion and confidentiality when handling sensitive information
- Minimum GCSE English and Mathematics, or equivalent qualifications

Role & Responsibilities

As a Legal Administrator, you will provide comprehensive administrative support to the Property team, helping fee earners manage transactions efficiently while maintaining excellent client service standards.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing day-to-day support across agricultural, commercial and residential property matters
- Managing diaries, appointments, key dates and transaction deadlines
- Preparing, formatting and proofreading legal correspondence, forms and property documentation
- Managing file opening and closing, compliance checks and client care documentation
- Maintaining accurate client records and matter information within the Practice Management System
- Ordering property searches, Land Registry documents and title information
- Assisting with Land Registry applications, completion packs and post-completion administration
- Preparing documents for signature, including using electronic signing platforms
- Supporting billing, time recording, expenses and other financial administration
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents, surveyors, lenders and other professional advisers
- Preparing client packs, transaction documents and bundles, maintaining organised electronic and paper files
- Providing flexible administrative support across the team while ensuring compliance with confidentiality and professional standards

Why Join?

This is an excellent opportunity to join a highly regarded specialist law firm offering a professional, supportive and collaborative working environment. You will gain exposure to a varied range of property matters while working closely with experienced legal professionals in a team that values quality, accuracy and exceptional client service.

title: Private Client Paralegal
description:
Thrive Group are delighted to working with a well-established and highly regarded high street firm in Chippenham. Are looking to recruit an experienced an Private Client Paralegal to join its friendly and close-knit team on a permanent basis.

What you will be doing:

You will manage a varied caseload of private client matters, providing practical advice and guidance to individuals and families on wills, probate, estate administration, Lasting Powers of Attorney and inheritance tax planning.
- Wills and estate planning: Taking instructions from clients, understanding their wishes and circumstances, drafting wills and advising on inheritance and succession planning.
- Probate and estate administration: Supporting executors and beneficiaries following a bereavement, preparing probate applications, gathering information on estate assets and liabilities, and assisting with the administration and distribution of estates.
- Lasting Powers of Attorney: Advising clients on LPAs for property and financial affairs and health and welfare, preparing documentation and managing the registration process.
- Inheritance Tax planning: Helping clients understand potential tax liabilities and exploring appropriate estate planning options to protect family wealth.
- Client relationship management: Building trusted relationships, explaining legal processes in clear, accessible language and providing a professional, empathetic service throughout.
- File management: Managing your own files from initial instruction through to completion, ensuring deadlines are met, records are accurate and matters progress efficiently.
- Wider private client support: Identifying additional planning needs and working collaboratively with colleagues to deliver a joined-up service to clients and their families.

What you will need to succeed
- At least three years' experience in private client work, ideally covering wills, probate, estate administration and LPAs.
- Experience managing your own caseload and progressing matters independently.
- A sound understanding of private client procedures and an interest in inheritance tax and estate planning.
- Excellent communication and client care skills, with a personable, empathetic and professional approach.
- The confidence to build lasting relationships and handle sensitive or complex family circumstances.
- A proactive, practical approach and the ability to work effectively as part of a small, supportive team.

Candidates working as a Private Client Fee Earner, Paralegal or experienced Private Client Executive may be well suited, depending on their level of experience and the scope of their current responsibilities.

What you will receive in return:
- Competitive salary and bonus structure.
- A stable, high-quality caseload from an established local client base
- A genuinely supportive and friendly team environment
- Opportunity to build long-term client relationships and grow your reputation locally
- 28 days' holiday plus bank holidays
- Monday to Friday, 9am-5pm working hours
- Real scope for progression as the firm continues to grow
